title: Time Series
tagline: Stationarity and autocorrelation, ARMA models, forecasting, unit roots, cointegration, vector autoregressions, volatility models and tests of asset-pricing models
summary: Economic and financial data arrive as sequences in time, with trends, cycles, persistence and changing volatility. This course develops the models used to describe and forecast them — stationary ARMA processes, forecasting and its evaluation, unit roots and cointegration, vector autoregressions and impulse responses — and the econometrics of financial returns, from volatility clustering and GARCH models to tests of asset-pricing models.

chapters.title: Stationarity and autocorrelation
chapters.summary: Time-series data, stationarity, autocovariance and autocorrelation functions, and white noise.

chapters.title: ARMA models
chapters.summary: Autoregressive and moving-average processes, their properties, identification and estimation.

chapters.title: Forecasting
chapters.summary: Optimal forecasts, forecast errors and intervals, model selection and the evaluation of forecasts.

chapters.title: Trends and unit roots
chapters.summary: Deterministic and stochastic trends, spurious regression and Dickey–Fuller tests.

chapters.title: Cointegration
chapters.summary: Long-run relationships between non-stationary series, error-correction models, and the Engle–Granger and Johansen methods.

chapters.title: Vector autoregressions
chapters.summary: VARs, Granger causality, impulse responses, variance decompositions and structural identification.

chapters.title: Volatility models
chapters.summary: Volatility clustering, ARCH and GARCH models, and realised volatility.

chapters.title: Testing asset-pricing models
chapters.summary: Return predictability, time-series and cross-sectional tests of factor models, and the generalised method of moments.
